topic: The Additive Property of Normal Distributions: Gaussian + Gaussian = Gaussian

sections.title: Introduction: The Intuition of Summing Randomness
lecture_lines: Imagine two robotic arms, each with placement errors.
Each arm’s error follows a bell-shaped distribution.
What happens when we add these errors together?
Visualize two separate normal curves side by side.
They represent independent sources of randomness.

sections.title: Prerequisites: Independence and Parameters
lecture_lines: A Gaussian distribution is defined by mean and variance.
Independence means one outcome doesn't affect another.
These are the essential building blocks for our sum.
animations: Show two separate, non-overlapping circles representing independent variables. (Color: #FFCC00)

sections.title: The Core Theorem: Adding the 'DNA'
lecture_lines: Adding independent Gaussians is surprisingly elegant.
The resulting mean is the sum of means.
The resulting variance is the sum of variances.
The two bell curves merge into one.
The final shape is always another Gaussian.
animations: Show the sum of means 'μ1 + μ2' appearing. (Color: #FFCC00)
Show the sum of variances 'σ1² + σ2²' appearing. (Color: #FFCC00)
Morph the two curves into a single, combined curve. (Color: #FF00FF)
Label the final curve with new mean and variance. (Color: #00FF00) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/dna.svg]

sections.title: Interactive Visualization: The Convolution Effect
lecture_lines: Summing random variables is mathematically a convolution.
Visually, we stack the probabilities together.
The final result is always a broader bell curve.
animations: Animate one Gaussian curve sliding over the other. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Show the area under both curves accumulating. (Color: #FFCC00)
Display the final broader, flatter Gaussian curve. (Color: #00FF00)

sections.title: Application and Conclusion
lecture_lines: This property simplifies modeling complex systems.
Just add parameters instead of using complex calculus.
Gaussian noise is universal in nature and engineering.
